record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Under what precise conditions do post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions converge, or at least approximate a global solution of the Einstein equations, possibly over a non-flat background metric?

evidence.quote: Show precise conditions under which the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions converge, or at least approximate, a global solution. It may be necessary to work with a non-flat background metric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the vacuum Einstein field equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$ (or the Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - 	frac{1}{2}R(g)\,g = T$ coupled to a suitable matter model) for a Lorentzian metric $g$ on a 4-manifold. Let $ ar g$ be a fixed background Lorentzian metric (for example the Minkowski metric $\eta$, or possibly a non-flat reference metric), and write a perturbative ansatz

$$ g \;=\;  ar g \;+\; \sum_{n\geq 1} \lambda^n\, h^{(n)}, $$

where $\lambda$ is a small parameter. Two standard choices are:

(i) The post-Minkowskian expansion: $\lambda = G$ (Newton's constant), so that the series is a formal power expansion in $G$ around a background $ ar g$ (typically Minkowski).

(ii) The post-Newtonian expansion: a joint expansion in $G$ and in $v/c$, where $v$ is a characteristic velocity and $c$ is the speed of light, so the metric components are expanded as formal series in powers of $1/c$.

In each case, the coefficients $h^{(n)}$ are determined recursively by linear wave-type equations on the background $ ar g$, subject to appropriate boundary conditions (asymptotic flatness, no incoming radiation from past null infinity, suitable matching between near zone and far zone).

Formulate precise sufficient conditions—on the matter source, on the background metric $ ar g$ (which may be allowed to be non-flat), on the initial/boundary data, and on the regime of validity in space-time—under which:

(a) the post-Newtonian formal series converges, in a specified function-space topology, to an exact global solution of the Einstein equations; or, failing that,

(b) the post-Newtonian series is an asymptotic expansion (in the sense of Poincaré) of a genuine global solution of the Einstein equations, with quantitative error estimates between the truncated series and the exact solution on prescribed space-time regions;

and analogously for the post-Minkowskian series in powers of $G$. Determine to what extent the use of a non-flat background metric $ ar g$ (rather than Minkowski) is necessary or helpful for establishing such convergence or asymptotic-approximation results.
artifact.status_search_result: The convergence (or even asymptotic nature) of the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions for the Einstein equations remains an open mathematical problem. Standard references (e.g., the Living Reviews article on post-Newtonian theory and surveys on PN/PM methods) explicitly note that there is no proof that the PN approximation is convergent or even asymptotic in a rigorous sense, although it is empirically extremely effective. Partial rigorous results exist (Damour, Rendall, Oliynyk, and others have established rigorous post-Newtonian approximations for fluid bodies under various restrictions), but no general precise conditions—particularly over non-flat backgrounds—are known.

status_evidence.title: Post-Newtonian theory for gravitational waves (Living Reviews)
status_evidence.snippet: The convergence of the PN series is not established; in practice the series is treated as an asymptotic expansion.
status_evidence.claim: Convergence of the post-Newtonian series is not rigorously established.

status_evidence.title: On the unreasonable effectiveness of the post-Newtonian approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Despite lack of proof of convergence or even of being asymptotic, PN approximations match numerical relativity remarkably well.
status_evidence.claim: The mathematical status of PN expansions as convergent/asymptotic series remains open.

status_evidence.title: Resumming Post-Minkowskian and Post-Newtonian gravitational waveform expansions
status_evidence.snippet: Resummation techniques are developed because the raw PN and PM series have unclear convergence properties.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research addresses but does not resolve the convergence of PM/PN expansions.
